text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN` when the input contains no parseable digits (e.g. `parseDigits("abc")`). It first tries `parseInt(str, 10)`, which is `NaN`; it then scans each character for Han decimal or other numbering-system digit ranges, accumulates nothing (leaving the accumulator as the empty string `""`), and finally returns `parseInt("", 10)`, which is `NaN`.

When the input doesn't match the regex, `match` returns the two-element array `[null, {}]`: the first element is the failed `String.prototype.match` result (`null`), and the second is an empty object of parsed values. Callers check the first element for truthiness (e.g. `if (matches)`), so `null` signals "no match" while the empty object means "no tokens extracted".

If the `eval(code)` call throws, `run` logs the error with `console.error(e)` and returns the string `"[error]"` (it does not rethrow). That string is what gets inserted into the example's result cell.

After all `example(...)` calls, the `examples` array (which by then holds one HTML `<tr class='example'>…</tr>` string per example, each containing the code, the `//=> ` divider and the `run(code)` result) is joined with `""` and appended to the `<table>` markup that is then assigned to `document.body.innerHTML`. The array itself is not cleared or otherwise modified.

`digitRegex` defaults to the Latin numbering system: it looks up `numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]`, and `numberingSystems.latn` is the regex fragment `\d`. So `digitRegex({})` returns `/\d/` (with `append` appended if given).

Still working on the `src/duration.js` bug behind "Duration#normalize can convert all unit pairs". I've reproduced failures (e.g. `years`↔`quarters`, `quarters`↔`seconds` produce NaN, and conversions that should leave a remainder in the target unit are dropped); fix ETA ~15 minutes.

Passing a falsy value (e.g. `""`, `null`, `undefined`) sets the module-level `defaultZone` variable to `null`, i.e. it resets the default zone back to the local zone (the `defaultZone` getter then falls back to `LocalZone.instance`). A truthy value is passed through `normalizeZone(z)` and stored instead.

When `matches.Z` is defined, `dateTimeFromMatches` sets the zone to `new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` — i.e. a fixed-offset zone built from the parsed offset value (the `Z` token's deserializer already converted the offset text into minutes). That zone is returned as the second element of the `[vals, zone]` pair. (For comparison: if `Z` is undefined but `matches.z` is defined it uses `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`, otherwise `zone` is `null`.)

Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly zero: `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)`. So `24:00:00.000` is accepted (the ISO end-of-day representation), while e.g. `24:00:00.001` or `24:30` is rejected with a `unit out of range` invalid for the hour.
`Zone#formatOffset(ts, format)` accepts three formats: `'narrow'` (e.g. `+6`), `'short'` (e.g. `+06:00`) and `'techie'` (e.g. `+0600`), as documented in its docstring.

Fixed and verified: `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` now pads negative numbers correctly (e.g. year -5 renders as `-0005`, not `00-5`), so `DateTime#toISODate()` pads negative years properly. Full suite still green apart from the two pre-existing locale failures.

Fixed and verified: `objToLocalTS` in `src/impl/util.js` now re-sets the year via `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of subtracting 1900 from the normalized year, so day overflow is re-normalized in the real (proleptic Gregorian) year. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({days: 61})` now gives 0100-03-02 (was 0100-03-01, off by one because 2000 is a leap year but 100 is not). A brute-force check of 100+ day offsets across the 100 barrier through February now matches the reference calendar exactly, and the suite is green.

Fixed and verified: `casualMatrix`/`accurateMatrix` in `src/duration.js` were missing the `years.quarters` (4) and `quarters.seconds` (91*24*60*60) entries, so `Duration#normalize` produced NaN for the years↔quarters and quarters↔seconds unit pairs. All 72 unit pairs now normalize correctly for both `casual` and `longterm` accuracy, and the existing normalize tests still pass.

Fixed and verified: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` instead of always `true`, so `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` is invalid and a DateTime in such a zone is itself invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Existing fixed-offset zone tests still pass.

Still working on the `src/datetime.js` bug behind "DateTime#isInDST() returns true for 1974 whole year in USA- from January 6th to October 27th". I've confirmed `isInDST` is currently false for all of 1974 in America/New_York (241 of 365 days wrong), because the January/May comparison dates keep the current day-of-month and 1974's DST started on January 6th. Fixed and verified: `isInDST` now compares the current offset against the offsets of January 1st and May 1st of the same year (`set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` / `set({ month: 5, day: 1 })`) instead of dates that kept the current day-of-month. Previously, for 1974 in the USA (DST ran Jan 6 – Oct 27) any date from Jan 6 on had its January counterpart also in DST, so `isInDST` was false for the entire year; now the whole Jan 6 – Oct 27 window reports true and the rest false (verified day-by-day for all of 1974 in America/New_York). The existing isInDST tests (pre/during/post-DST, UTC/fixed offsets, invalid) all still pass, and the full suite shows only the two pre-existing locale failures.
